initial.charge: Production sprite sheet for a 2D chibi Three Kingdoms RPG. Use the ATTACHED IMAGE ONLY AS CHARACTER DESIGN AND PAINTING STYLE REFERENCE. Match its richly hand-painted dark blue armor, gold filigree, huge expressive head, blue helmet plume, warm shaded skin, thick brown outlines and cute proportions EXACTLY. NOT minimalist vector art. Output exactly SIX animation frames on one 3-column by 2-row atlas, landscape 1536x1024 ideal. Reading order top-left to top-right then bottom-left to bottom-right. Every cell exactly equal size. Each full character including ALL weapons, plume, feet, horse tail, torch flame must stay inside its own cell with 12% empty transparent padding EVERY side. Same camera, same scale, same costume details, same weapon length, same facing RIGHT three-quarter side view, same cell-relative ground line and root position throughout all SIX frames. True transparent alpha background, no scenery, no text, no numbers, no dividers, no cast shadows, no checkerboard drawn in. This must be a legible six-POSE animation, poses must change convincingly (NOT six identical portraits). Last frame must lead naturally back to first for cyclic playback. Keep sprites separated by wide transparent gutters. Animate ONLY the reference upper-right mounted cavalry soldier on his stout brown horse. A continuous RUN-IN-PLACE gallop cycle, rider crouched forward with spear pointed right, all mounted frames, no infantry or dismounting. Frame 1: front legs reaching forward, hind legs extended rearward, low suspended extended stride. Frame 2: leading front hoof contacts ground, shoulders absorb weight, hind legs begin folding forward. Frame 3: front legs push backward under chest, hind legs tucked forward beneath belly, rider dips subtly with saddle. Frame 4: hind hooves push off under body, front knees lift and fold, compact gathered airborne silhouette. Frame 5: body rises, front legs unfold forward, hind legs sweep back, mane and plume trail left. Frame 6: approaching extended stride again, front legs almost forward but slightly bent, rear legs almost extended, position leads smoothly into frame1. Draw four anatomically coherent horse legs, exactly one rider seated on same saddle, complete horse in every cell. Rider's hands stay gripping same spear shaft and reins, rider never floats away from saddle.
